*** DOES THE PARENT-CAPABILITY DEFECT SPREAD? NO. ***
create_custom_field_dataset_v2's response declares data.options as an array and always returns it as an empty object {}, even though the options it just created are genuinely persisted (confirmed only by a follow-up read). This sibling capability does NOT share that bug: the create response for option 146670 came back with data = {id, option_value, is_default, colour, parent_option_id} exactly as declared — id 146670 populated, option_value echoed verbatim, is_default echoed as sent (true), colour null (nothing was sent for it), parent_option_id null (flat dropdown, not nested). Every declared field present, nothing extra. Contract is a clean PASS, zero declared_missing, zero undeclared_returned. So the write-response-lies-about-its-own-result bug is specific to create_custom_field_dataset (the multi-option dataset-create call), not a single serializer shared across the whole dataset-option surface — this single-option create call DOES let a caller learn the new option's id directly from the response, which is exactly what update_custom_field_dataset_option needs.

*** DUPLICATE-OPTION QUESTION — THIRD (AND FOURTH) INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION ***
Read dataset 31320's options back two ways after the create:
  1. list_custom_field_dataset_options(106131, 31320) → 3 rows, ids 146670/146669/146668, each exactly once.
  2. get_custom_field_dataset(106131, 31320, fetch_options=true) → same 3 rows, each exactly once, this time with the fuller row shape (group_id, project_id, custom_field_id, dataset_id, record_status, created_at, updated_at).
No duplication in either read. Combined with the two prior independent creation-path confirmations (field-definition-create and dataset-create), this is now a fourth confirmation via two additional read paths: newly created custom-field options come back exactly once, cleanly. Safe to tell the product team the priority (8/4), status (10/5), case_type (22/11) doubling on the old default fields is historical data, not a live serializer artifact — four independent observations across creation and read paths agree.

*** DISCRIMINATOR — CONFIRMED PRESENT ***
The create response itself (data shape: id, option_value, is_default, colour, parent_option_id) does NOT carry record_status/created_at/updated_at/dataset_id — that response shape is fixed and minimal, matching describeCapability's declared 200 exactly. But reading the option back through get_custom_field_dataset(fetch_options=true) shows the full stored row:
  {id:146670, group_id:3452, project_id:null, custom_field_id:106131, dataset_id:31320, option_value:'__mcp-probe-cfoption-20260921', is_default:true, parent_option_id:null, record_status:'active', created_at:'2026-09-21T13:47:13.000Z', updated_at:'2026-09-21T13:47:13.000Z'}
So yes: the new option carries record_status:'active' plus created_at/updated_at/dataset_id, confirmed on the stored row (not on the create response, which is deliberately thin) — consistent with the discriminator already seen on options 146668/146669 and on the sibling field's earlier probe. The old default-field rows (priority/status/case_type) still carry none of this.

*** IS_DEFAULT SEMANTICS — ANSWERED: OLD DEFAULT IS SILENTLY DEMOTED ***
Before this probe, dataset 31320's default was option 146668 (is_default:true, updated_at = its creation time 13:34:12). This probe created option 146670 with is_default:true while 146668 was still the default. Reading the dataset back afterward shows:
  - 146670: is_default:true (the new option, as sent)
  - 146668: is_default:**false**, updated_at bumped to 13:47:13 (the moment of THIS create call) — its value was mutated as a side effect, even though this call's path/body never named option 146668 at all.
  - 146669: unaffected, still is_default:false, updated_at unchanged from dataset creation.
So on this CREATE path the answer is: the old default is auto-demoted server-side, not left as a second default and not rejected. Nobody ends up with two defaults on this path. This is worth flagging against the sibling update_custom_field_dataset_option's own guidance, which states the OPPOSITE for the UPDATE call: 'Making an option the default does not clear the previous default; on a single-select dropdown clear the old one yourself.' If that guidance is accurate, the two sibling write calls have genuinely different default-demotion semantics — create auto-demotes, update does not — which is itself worth confirming directly when update_custom_field_dataset_option is probed, rather than assumed to match this call's behavior.

*** UNBLOCKING update_custom_field_dataset_option ***
Reporting the new option id prominently: **option id = 146670**, on dataset_id = 31320, custom_fields_id = 106131, currently option_value = '__mcp-probe-cfoption-20260921', is_default = true (the current live default of dataset 31320, having demoted 146668). This is a clean single-option target for the update probe: no parent_option_id (flat dropdown, not nested), colour null, not yet touched by any update call.
Options are added ONE AT A TIME by this capability — the body is a single option_value/is_default/parent_option_id triple, not an array or a full-set replace (contrast with create_custom_field_dataset, which takes an `options` array at dataset-creation time only). So update_custom_field_dataset_option necessarily also targets a single option (its own path carries a third id segment beyond custom_fields_id/dataset_id, presumably option_id) — there is no full-set replace semantics anywhere on this surface to worry about; each option is an independently addressable row from creation through update through delete.
